title: Chicherin → Sukhanov (Vladivostok Soviet): telegram on routing Allied consular telegrams via Moscow, with code passages unread by AEF Siberia
correspondents: G. V. Chicherin, People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs → K. A. Sukhanov, President of the Vladivostok Soviet
shelfmark: NARA RG 395, AEF Siberia historical files, microfilm M917 roll 3 (file unit naId 337858938), frames M917-003-0350 to 0354 (Intelligence Summary No. 27, 8 Nov 1918, with Capt. F. B. Rives' memorandum of 6 Nov 1918)
folio_note: Only the translation is filmed (frame 0353, 'Moscow #00784'), with '(code from hereon)' and '(more code)' where the code passages stood. Rives says the 'exact copy of the telegram as received' was held by the AEF intelligence office; a copy went to the Director of Military Intelligence, Washington.
status: AEF Siberia memorandum: 'The code and cipher section inform that they are not in position to solve by inspection the short passages of code contained in the message'; the key was presumed destroyed with Sukhanov's papers. The ciphertext itself is not on the reel; it may survive in the MID copy (RG 165) or the AEF intelligence files. The same memorandum describes 18 Allied telegrams (16 American, many 'wholly or partly in code') abstracted from the Vladivostok telegraph office; those are US/Allied traffic copies, not a separate candidate. Not in catalogue.json (known.py: no hits for Chicherin, Sukhanov).
why: A Soviet foreign-commissariat code telegram of spring 1918 tied to the Mirbach/German-control allegations; the unread passages name the routing after Brest-Litovsk. Its authenticity should be checked against the Sisson-document controversy.
prior_art: open (checked 27 Oct 2026: catalogue.json/known.py; no web search)

folio_note: Roll 83 frames 0692-1550 (target 2 starts at frame 0692). Ciphertext circulars in 2-digit bigram-key groups: f.0696-0697 (15 Dec 1906), 0698 (10 Mar 1910, No. 63637), 0712 (18 Jun 1902, No. 281), 0732 (1895, No. 4945), 0742-0743 (No. 416), 0749 (1891, No. 3313), 0751-0752 (13 Aug 1891, No. 3902, c. 330 groups, viewed: clean, no interlinear), 0755-0757 (22 Mar 1895, No. 5078), 0769-0770 (10 Mar 1895, No. 5015), 0774 (31 Dec 1904, No. 1201), 0818-0820 (May/Jul 1897, Nos. 5657, 5700), 0823, 0835-0836, 0842, 0847, 0849; the consulate's replies in cipher f.0733-0735 (No. 519, 1895, Olarovsky); 5-digit secret circular No. 864 "aux Ambassades, Légations, Consulats" f.0703-0705 (c. 350 groups, viewed: clean, groups split by hand into 3-figure parts); 5-digit cables f.0694 (cable No. 63, 22 Oct 1908), 0800-0801, 0880-0882 (Oustinoff); naval-ministry letter cipher f.0805-0807 (5-letter groups with a repeating 2849284928... key line and Russian clear text: decrypted). Key material on the same roll: instructions and worked examples for the bigram keys No. 381 (1893; f.0780-0793) and No. 389 (1900; f.0713-0727, with the 12 Dec 1865 "Pesth" example in plaintext, transposition sheet and cipher), circular on key No. 400 (1905; f.0731), additions to the dictionary key No. 402 (1910; f.0728, 0802-0803), lozungi to recipher key No. 448 "Lambda" (1915; f.0869), rules on keeping keys (f.0759-0764), Naval Ministry cipher No. 383 (f.0863-0865) and Naval key No. 394 instructions plus dictionary (f.0884-0900, 0928-1073), and decode tables (f.1088-1550, "Разборная таблица No. 404" f.1443).
status: Found in the RG 64 bulk_all hits (frames with 2-digit groups in a Russian consulate file); full roll OCR read and two frames viewed (0703, 0751). Some circulars carry the consulate's letter-by-letter decipherment worksheets on the following frames (f.0706-0711 after No. 864; 0758, 0772, 0776, 0794-0796, 0822-0825, 0837), so part of the run was read at the time; others show no worksheet in the OCR of the adjacent frames (1891 No. 3902, 1895 Nos. 4945 and 5078, 1906, 1910). The cipher system is described in full on the roll (bigram table + transposition "transparents" Lit. A/B/D; 3-figure values regrouped in 5s for the telegraph), and keys 381/389 come with plaintext-ciphertext examples. Not on DECODE; known.py: no hit for M1486, Olarovsky, Russian Consulate. Not in catalogue.json or any nara_* folder. || Brackx, issue #167 (28 Oct 2026): M1486 roll 83 (target 2, frames 0692-1550): the system is a bigram-table scheme (stencils A and D; instructions to keys 381 and 389, worked example 0790-0792); only key No. 404's tables are filmed (frames 1440-1446), so the 1888-1905 circulars' keys 356, 375, 381, 389 are not filmed; later circulars were deciphered at the time. Not checked on the film here.
why: A run of tsarist Foreign Ministry cipher circulars to a consulate, filed with the consulate's own key instructions and worksheets: rare primary evidence of Russian diplomatic bigram ciphers and naval codes of 1890-1910, and the unread circulars can be tested against keys and worked examples on the same roll.
